parsed.thesis: Critical go/no-go checks must not rest on human vigilance. When a consequential decision depends on verification, the check itself should be made structural: encoded as an executable gate that produces auditable pass/fail evidence and blocks the transition on failure, so correctness follows from the system's design rather than from a person remembering to look — and the gate should be built only after observable evidence confirms which failure mechanism actually needs guarding.

principleCandidate.title: Encode critical verification as executable, evidence-producing gates, not manual checks
principleCandidate.rationale: The root cause across all Dreamer candidates is that manual verification lets omissions pass silently: completion by a human is treated as success, no structured evidence is produced, and pain surfaces only downstream. Encoding each verification step as a rule-based check with structured pass/fail output, a blocking transition on failure, and persisted provenance removes reliance on human attention, makes every run reproducible and auditable, and converts the hard constraint into a structural property of the system rather than a procedural hope.
principleCandidate.scope: Applies whenever a consequential transition (graduation, release, promotion, approval, deployment) is gated by verification that currently relies on manual human checking, implicit procedural knowledge, or assertion-based completion. Especially relevant when omission carries meaningful downside, when evidence of the check must be auditable after the fact, and when the check can be expressed as deterministic rules. Not applicable where verification genuinely requires human judgment that cannot be formalized.

risks: Partially duplicates and synthesizes existing core axioms T-05 (guardrail encoding) and T-07 (verify after act); adding it to the axiom set risks redundancy unless it is treated as an operational refinement rather than a new axiom.

Premature automation risk: as the Dreamer's own evidence_before_inference candidate notes, encoding checks before observable evidence confirms the actual failure mechanism can formalize and entrench the wrong problem.

Automated gates can drift from actual intent over time; a passing gate may be wrongly treated as proof of correctness while the checks themselves become stale, brittle, or cargo-culted, inverting into false confidence.

Hard-blocking transitions on any single failed check without severity calibration can halt legitimate progress on low-signal or non-critical failures, creating new friction and workarounds that undermine the gate.
Full provenance and structured logging for every check add persistence and maintenance overhead that may be disproportionate for low-stakes verifications.

principleDraft.rationale: Manual verification lets omissions pass silently: a human's completion is treated as success, no structured evidence is produced, and pain surfaces only downstream. Encoding each check as a rule-based gate with structured pass/fail output, a blocking transition on failure, and persisted provenance removes reliance on human attention, makes every run reproducible and auditable, and converts the hard constraint into a structural property of the system rather than a procedural hope. Grounding the gate in prior observable evidence of the actual failure mechanism prevents premature automation of the wrong check.
applicability: Consequential transitions gated by verification: release, deployment, promotion, graduation, approval
Verification that currently relies on manual human checking, implicit procedural knowledge, or assertion-based completion
Circumstances where a missed check carries meaningful downstream downside or the check must be auditable after the fact
Checks that can be expressed as deterministic, rule-based conditions
antiPatterns: Relying on a human 'sign-off' or 'looks good' as the sole control on a consequential transition
Treating an assertion of completion (e.g., 'done, I checked it') as verification evidence
Manual checklists that leave no structured, persisted pass/fail record or provenance
Allowing a consequential transition to proceed when a required check failed or was skipped
Encoding gates speculatively before observable evidence confirms which failure mechanism they must guard
Treating a passing gate as permanent proof of correctness without revisiting whether its checks still match intent

intentContract.targetBehavior: Before executing a consequential transition, the agent runs an executable gate covering the required checks, records structured pass/fail output with persisted provenance, and aborts the transition when any check fails; a new gate is only encoded after observable evidence identifies the failure mechanism it guards.
intentContract.forbiddenBehavior: Proceeding on a consequential transition based on manual inspection, verbal or written assertion of completion, or unrecorded human sign-off — any go/no-go decision that rests on human vigilance instead of a blocking, evidence-producing check.
intentContract.evidenceSource: The consolidated Dreamer/Philosopher diagnosis that manual verification lets omissions pass silently: human completion is treated as success, no structured evidence is produced, and pain surfaces only downstream.
intentContract.validationExpectation: An evaluator should accept a rule as faithful only if it mandates (1) executable checks producing structured pass/fail output, (2) a blocking transition on failure, (3) persisted provenance of each gate run, and (4) observable evidence of the failure mechanism before a gate is encoded; any proposed change that removes blocking, evidence output, or the evidence-before-encoding requirement contradicts this intent and must be flagged.

risks: Substantial overlap with core axioms T-05 (translate hard constraints into explicit guardrails and forbidden transitions) and T-07 (observe results after acting); this principle should be treated as an operational refinement of those axioms, not a new axiom, to avoid redundancy.
The evidence-before-encoding requirement overlaps T-03 (use observable evidence before inferring); premature automation can formalize and entrench the wrong failure mechanism.
Automated gates can drift from actual intent over time; a passing gate may be treated as proof of correctness while its checks become stale, brittle, or cargo-culted, inverting into false confidence.
Hard-blocking transitions on any single failed check without severity calibration can halt legitimate progress on low-signal or non-critical failures, creating workarounds that undermine the gate.
Persisted provenance and structured logging for every check add persistence and maintenance overhead that may be disproportionate for low-stakes verifications.
Some verifications genuinely require human judgment that cannot be formalized; forcing executable gates in those cases yields box-ticking compliance rather than real verification.

principleDraft.title: Encode go/no-go verification as executable, evidence-producing gates that block on failure
principleDraft.statement: Before a consequential transition (graduation, release, promotion, approval, deployment) may pass, every verification step gating it must be encoded as an executable, rule-based check that (a) is grounded in observable evidence of the actual failure mechanism rather than an assumed one, (b) emits a structured, persisted pass/fail record on every run, and (c) structurally blocks the transition on failure. The transition may be declared successful only when the gate's recorded evidence matches the intended outcome — never when a manual check is merely reported as completed.
principleDraft.rationale: The diagnosed root cause is that PRI-650-A Gate B graduation verification was designed to rely on manual human checking with no automated gate or rule-based validation, so omissions pass silently, human completion is treated as success, no structured evidence is produced, and pain surfaces only downstream via CLI reports without host trace. Encoding the check as an executable gate makes correctness a structural property of the system instead of a product of human vigilance: every run becomes reproducible and auditable, failures intercept the transition before it executes, and reconciliation against the intended outcome replaces assertion-based completion. Requiring observable evidence of the failure mechanism before building the gate guards against formalizing the wrong problem, which matters because the diagnosis explicitly flags thin evidence (a single owner_reported:cli entry with no session context and an unconfirmed failure mode).
applicability: Consequential transitions gated by verification that currently depends on manual human checking, implicit procedural knowledge, or assertion-based completion (e.g., PRI-650-A Gate B graduation, release, promotion, approval, deployment)
Verification steps whose omission carries meaningful downside and must be intercepted before the transition executes, and whose checks can be expressed as deterministic rules with auditable results
Out of scope: verifications that irreducibly require human judgment that cannot be formalized, and low-stakes checks where gate and logging overhead is disproportionate
antiPatterns: Gating a consequential transition on manual human checking with no executable, rule-based check in place
Accepting a human assertion that a verification was performed (or merely completed) as proof of verification success
Letting the transition proceed when a gate check fails, deferring detection to downstream pain reports
Running verification without producing or persisting a structured pass/fail record, leaving the run unauditable
Building an automated gate from an assumed failure mechanism without observable evidence (logs, traces, tool outputs) confirming which check is actually needed

intentContract.ownerIntent: The Owner wants consequential go/no-go verifications such as PRI-650-A Gate B graduation to pass only on executable, rule-based checks with auditable pass/fail evidence — never on a person having manually performed (or reported performing) the check.
intentContract.targetBehavior: When designing or operating a gated verification, the agent first gathers observable evidence of the actual failure mechanism, then encodes each check as an executable rule that emits and persists a structured pass/fail record, structurally blocks the gated transition on failure, and declares success only when the recorded evidence matches the intended outcome.
intentContract.forbiddenBehavior: A consequential transition passing because a manual verification step was reported as completed — with no executable check, no structured pass/fail record, and no structural blocking — or a gate being built on an assumed, evidence-unconfirmed failure mechanism.
intentContract.evidenceSource: diagnosis_manual_1788424714466_wmn09nli: Gate B graduation verification designed as manual checking with no automated gate or rule-based validation (violated T-03/T-05/T-07); the only behavioral evidence was a single owner_reported:cli pain report with owner_reported_no_host_trace and 'No session context available'; ambiguity notes state the concrete failure mechanism (missing automation vs. missing check scripts vs. redundant manual steps) remains unconfirmed.
intentContract.validationExpectation: An evaluator should accept a rule as faithful only if it requires, for every consequential gated transition: (1) an executable check with structured pass/fail output, (2) a persisted run record, (3) structural blocking of the transition on failure, (4) success declared on evidence matching intent rather than manual completion, and (5) observable confirmation of the failure mechanism before the gate is built. Any change that allows manual-completion-based passage, removes the blocking behavior, or drops the evidence-first precondition contradicts this intent and must be flagged rather than implemented.

risks: Overlaps with core axioms T-05 (translate hard constraints into executable guardrails and forbidden transitions) and T-07 (observe results and compare with intended outcome); this draft must be treated as an operational refinement combining them for gated transitions, not as a new independent axiom.

Premature automation: the source evidence is thin (a single owner_reported:cli report with no host trace and an unconfirmed failure mechanism), so encoding gates before confirming the actual mechanism can formalize and entrench the wrong problem.

Gate drift and false confidence: passing gates may be treated as proof of correctness while the checks themselves become stale, brittle, or cargo-culted, inverting the principle into an illusion of verification.
Uncalibrated hard-blocking on any single failed check can halt legitimate progress on low-signal or non-critical failures, breeding bypass workarounds that undermine the gate.
Persisting structured records and provenance for every check adds maintenance overhead disproportionate for low-stakes verifications; applicability must stay limited to consequential transitions.

This principle does not repair the upstream reporting-path gap (pain reported via CLI with no authenticated host session provenance), which limits the quality of evidence available to satisfy the gate-building precondition.

parsed.thesis: Critical validations that depend on human diligence rather than structural enforcement are inherently fragile. The Dreamer's candidates converge on one insight: hard constraints (e.g., graduation criteria) become trustworthy only when translated into executable, self-enforcing automated gates that emit persistent, structured pass/fail evidence; execution by itself is not verification until actual results are reconciled against expected criteria; and recurring severe manual friction is not an operational nuisance to be endured but a design-defect signal demanding structural redesign rather than repeated human effort.

principleCandidate.title: Convert recurring manual verification of hard constraints into automated, self-enforcing, evidence-emitting gates
principleCandidate.rationale: The root cause was that graduation criteria existed only as implicit process knowledge executed via manual checking, so human omission had no structural barrier and produced no auditable result record. Automated gate checks eliminate the omission risk, persisted structured results make every verification observable and re-checkable, and the recurrence of severe manual pain itself becomes the trigger for this structural migration rather than a cue to repeat the manual effort.
principleCandidate.scope: Applies wherever a hard constraint, gate, or acceptance criterion is verified primarily through manual human checking, especially when the same manual friction recurs across sessions (release gates, merge/graduation checks, compliance validations, recurring manual sign-offs). Less applicable to one-off validations or genuinely judgment-based evaluations.

risks: Overlaps significantly with core axiom T-05 (constraints as explicit guardrails and forbidden transitions) and T-08 (friction as feedback); its only distinct contribution is linking pain recurrence to guardrail automation, so it may duplicate rather than extend existing axioms

Automated gates may reject valid edge cases requiring human judgment; an unauditable human-override path can reintroduce the original omission risk the automation was meant to remove
For low-frequency checks, building automation may violate T-06 (simplest intervention) — automation cost must be justified by recurrence and severity of the manual pain
Automated gate outputs can create false confidence if not themselves verified against ground truth (T-07); a broken check that always passes is worse than manual verification

principleDraft.title: Automate recurring manual verification of hard constraints as blocking, evidence-emitting gates
principleDraft.statement: Whenever a hard constraint or acceptance criterion (graduation, release, merge, compliance, sign-off gates) is verified primarily by manual human checking — especially when the same severe manual friction recurs — convert that verification into an executable, self-enforcing automated gate: encode each criterion as an explicit check, block the gated transition until the check passes, and emit a persistent structured pass/fail record that is reconciled against the expected criteria. Manual review may remain only as a supplementary check after the automated gate passes, never as the sole barrier; recurrence of severe manual pain on the same gate is the trigger for this structural migration, not a cue to repeat the manual effort.
principleDraft.rationale: The diagnosed root cause was that graduation criteria existed only as implicit process knowledge executed via manual checking: human omission had no structural barrier and produced no auditable result record, and completion of manual verification was never reconciled against the expected criteria. Encoding criteria as executable blocking checks removes the omission risk; persisting structured pass/fail results makes every verification observable, re-checkable, and reconcilable (execution is not success until results are compared with intent); and treating recurring severe manual friction as a design-defect signal for structural migration stops the system from repeatedly paying the same manual cost for the same flaw.
applicability: Hard-constraint gates and acceptance criteria currently verified by manual human checking (e.g., PRI-650-A Gate B graduation verification, release gates, merge checks, compliance validations, recurring manual sign-offs)
Situations where the same manual verification friction recurs across sessions with severe impact
Constraints that are objectively expressible as checkable criteria (objective pass/fail standards)
Out of scope: one-off validations and genuinely judgment-based evaluations that cannot be encoded as executable checks
antiPatterns: Passing a hard-constraint gate on manual inspection alone, with no executable check and no persisted pass/fail record
Treating completion of a manual verification as success without reconciling actual results item-by-item against the expected criteria
Leaving hard constraints as implicit process knowledge or documentation with nothing that structurally blocks the gated transition when criteria are unmet
Responding to recurring severe manual verification pain by repeating the same manual effort instead of automating the check
Automation without evidence: a gate that emits no persistent structured result, or whose always-pass behavior is never verified against ground truth

intentContract.targetBehavior: When the agent encounters a hard-constraint gate verified manually (especially with recurring severe friction), it builds or requires an executable automated check that evaluates each criterion, blocks the gated action on failure, and writes a structured pass/fail log reconciled against the expected criteria; any manual review happens only after the gate passes.
intentContract.forbiddenBehavior: Allowing a hard-constraint gate to be passed solely by human diligence — manual execution with no automated barrier, no structural blocking when criteria are unmet, and no persisted structured result for reconciliation — and repeating that manual effort each time the pain recurs.

principleDraft.title: Convert Recurring Manual Verification of Hard Constraints into Automated Evidence-Emitting Gates
principleDraft.statement: Whenever a hard constraint (gate, acceptance criterion, or compliance check) is verified primarily through recurring manual human checking, it must be migrated into an automated, self-enforcing gate that executes the check mechanically and persists a structured pass/fail result; the constraint may be declared satisfied only by reconciling that persisted evidence against the expected criteria — never by assuming a manual step was diligently performed.
principleDraft.rationale: The diagnosed root cause was that hard constraints existed as implicit process knowledge executed via manual checking, so human omission had no structural barrier and left no auditable result record. Automating the check removes dependence on human diligence, and persisting structured pass/fail evidence makes every verification observable, re-checkable, and reconcilable against intended criteria. Recurrence of severe manual friction is treated as the design-defect signal that triggers this structural migration, rather than as an operational cost to be repeatedly paid.
applicability: Release gates, merge checks, and graduation/deployment criteria currently verified by manual human checking
Recurring compliance or security validations executed against a fixed, codable rubric or schedule
Recurring manual sign-offs where the checker follows a mechanical rubric rather than exercised judgment
Any hard constraint whose dominant failure mode is 'the human forgot or skipped the check'
antiPatterns: Re-executing the same manual checklist across sessions while treating the friction as normal operational cost
Declaring a hard constraint satisfied based on the assumption that a manual step was performed, with no persisted pass/fail record
Gates whose results exist only in transient console output with no persistent, structured, re-checkable record
Silent human overrides of a failed gate without an audited override record
Automating a constraint before its criteria are sufficiently modeled, enshroring wrong criteria in a structurally enforcing gate

intentContract.ownerIntent: The Owner wants hard constraints like graduation criteria enforced by automated, self-enforcing gates that persist structured pass/fail evidence, instead of depending on a human remembering to run a manual check.
intentContract.targetBehavior: On the second or later occurrence of manually verifying the same hard constraint, the agent implements an automated gate that executes the check and writes a structured pass/fail result to a persistent artifact, then cites that record — reconciled against the expected criteria — as the verification evidence.
intentContract.forbiddenBehavior: Repeatedly performing the same manual verification of a hard constraint across sessions and marking the constraint satisfied without any persisted, machine-checkable pass/fail record.
intentContract.evidenceSource: Diagnosis that graduation criteria existed only as implicit process knowledge checked manually, so human omission had no structural barrier and produced no auditable result record (philosopher artifact pi-art-philosopher-pri815-G-manual_1788424714466_wmn-r2-run1, distilling the Dreamer's recurring-manual-friction insight).
intentContract.validationExpectation: An evaluator should accept a rule only if it (a) triggers on recurrence of a mechanical manual check of a hard constraint, (b) requires an automated gate that persists a structured pass/fail record, and (c) requires reconciling that record against expected criteria before declaring satisfaction; rules that mandate automating one-off or judgment-based checks, or that merely restate T-05/T-08 without the recurrence-trigger or evidence-emission delta, should be rejected as duplicative or unfaithful.

risks: Substantial overlap with core axiom T-05 (constraints as explicit guardrails) and T-08 (friction as feedback); the distinct delta is only the recurrence trigger plus the persistent structured-evidence requirement, so downstream rule generation must scope rules to that delta to avoid duplicating existing axioms

Premature automation can fossilize an incompletely understood constraint (conflicts with T-01): automating before sufficiently modeling the criteria can enshrine wrong checks that structurally block legitimate work
Automated gates may reject valid edge cases requiring human judgment; an unauditable or silent human-override path reintroduces the very omission risk the automation was meant to remove
For low-frequency checks, building automation violates T-06 (simplest intervention); migration must be justified by demonstrated recurrence and severity of the manual pain
A faulty gate that always passes creates false confidence worse than manual checking (T-07); the gate's own correctness must be verified against ground truth at least once after construction
If 'structured' and 'persistent' are left loosely defined, agents may satisfy the letter (a transient log line) while missing the spirit (re-checkable evidence)

principleDraft.statement: Whenever a consequential state transition (release, promotion, sign-off, deployment, graduation, merge approval) is conditioned on verification criteria, encode each criterion as an executable check wired into a structural gate that blocks the transition on failure; then reconcile the logged results against the expected outcomes and persist the evidence with provenance (what ran, when, under whose authority) in durable storage outside transient context. Manual attestation alone must never authorize such a transition. Criteria that are genuinely subjective must be explicitly marked as recorded human-judgment items, not silently skipped or forced into brittle rules.
principleDraft.rationale: The diagnosed root cause was not a lack of diligence but a verification mechanism whose authority rested on human attestation rather than executable evidence. Manual gates fail in four characteristic ways: steps get omitted, reviewer judgment drifts, completion claims are never reconciled against the actual criteria, and results evaporate with transient context. Encoding criteria as executable checks removes omission and drift; the structural guardrail makes passage impossible without execution (per T-05); reconciling logged results against expectations converts assumed success into demonstrated success (per T-03 and T-07); and persisting evidence with provenance makes the record auditable after the verifying context is gone (per T-10).
applicability: Hard state transitions conditioned on verification criteria: releases, deployments, promotions, sign-offs, merge approvals, graduations
Pipelines, CI/CD gates, and multi-actor workflows where manual checklists, remembered procedures, or transient session context are the current default
Any workflow where completion is currently demonstrated by human attestation ('I checked it') rather than machine-reconciled evidence
Audit or compliance contexts where evidence of what was verified, by what, and when must outlive the session that verified it
antiPatterns: Authorizing a consequential transition on manual attestation, memory, or a checked checklist item with no executable check behind it
Treating a check as passed simply because it ran, without reconciling its logged output against the declared criteria
Leaving verification results only in transient context (chat history, terminal scrollback, reviewer memory) with no durable record or provenance
Keeping verification criteria as an implicit or remembered procedure rather than codified, executable checks under structural guardrail
Silently dropping criteria that resist automation instead of explicitly marking them as recorded human-judgment items
Bypassing the gate for expedience or emergencies without recording the bypass, its justification, and who authorized it
